# TexasBitcoin

> The authority on Bitcoin in Texas: the energy and mining base layer, the money law, and the programmable-money frontier being built on top. An independent research and reference publication — every datable claim is sourced to primary documents or reputable journalism. Not financial, investment, legal, or tax advice.

## Core reference

- [The History of Bitcoin in Texas](https://texasbitcoin.com/history-of-bitcoin-in-texas): The definitive, sourced account — from Supervisory Memorandum 1037 (2014) through the mining migration to Rockdale (2021), ERCOT demand response, and the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve (SB 21, 2025). 21 cited sources.
- [What Texas Law Actually Says About Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/what-texas-law-says-about-bitcoin): The legal status of Bitcoin in Texas from the primary record — legal to buy, sell, hold, and mine; no state license to sell your own coin (Supervisory Memorandum 1037); custody, UCC, proof of reserves, legal tender vs. reserve asset, taxes, and the federal 18 U.S.C. § 1960 seam. 13 cited sources.
- [The Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-strategic-bitcoin-reserve): How the state's Bitcoin reserve works and where it stands — SB 21 (signed June 20, 2025), the $10M appropriation, the $500B market-cap floor, the first ~$5M purchase via the iShares Bitcoin Trust (November 20, 2025), the five-member advisory committee, and the move from a Bitcoin ETF to direct custody. A tracked reference. 7 cited sources.
- [Elon Musk, Tesla, and the Bitcoin Energy Question](https://texasbitcoin.com/elon-musk-bitcoin-energy): The sourced account of Tesla's Bitcoin treasury (the $1.5B purchase, Feb 2021; accepting then suspending BTC payments over energy, May 2021; the ~75% sale for $936M, Q2 2022; 11,509 BTC still held in 2026 — all from SEC filings), Musk's 2021 energy reversal and the Cambridge index (cbeci.org) he shared, the greening of Bitcoin's energy mix (Cambridge: 52.4% sustainable in 2025) with its honest counterweight, and how Musk's own AI data centers (xAI's Colossus) now dwarf Bitcoin's energy use — colliding with Bitcoin mining on the Texas ERCOT grid. 28 cited sources.
- [Ross Ulbricht, Silk Road, and Bitcoin's First Use Case](https://texasbitcoin.com/ross-ulbricht-silk-road-bitcoin): The sourced account of the Austin-born (UT Dallas physics, 2006) founder of Silk Road — Bitcoin's first application at scale (Tor + Bitcoin, 2011–2013, mostly illegal drugs) — kept honest about what Silk Road was. Arrest (Oct 1, 2013), conviction on all seven counts (Feb 4, 2015), the two-life-plus-40-years sentence under Judge Katherine Forrest, the precise murder-for-hire record (alleged, never charged/tried/convicted, no one killed), the seized Bitcoin (~174,000 BTC auctioned 2014–15; the separate 69,370 BTC seized 2020, now in the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve), the Free Ross campaign led by his mother Lyn Ulbricht (~607,000-signature petition), and the full and unconditional pardon (Jan 21, 2025) and Bitcoin 2025 speech. Includes the primary video of his post-pardon keynote. 28 cited sources.
- [Ted Cruz and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/ted-cruz-bitcoin): Did Ted Cruz fall out of Bitcoin, or sell out? The sourced record answers: from self-described skeptic ("I didn't understand it very much," Oct 2021) to the Senate's loudest champion — the Aug 9, 2021 infrastructure-bill floor fight ("not greater than five" senators could define a cryptocurrency), disclosed purchases (up to $50,000 on Jan 25, 2022, via River; $50,001–$100,000 in 2023), the CBDC Anti-Surveillance State Act (S. 3801, Feb 2024), the Commerce Committee chairmanship (Jan 2025), the FLARE Act (S. 1188, Mar 2025), and the four-year CBDC ban that became law July 11, 2026 (Public Law 119-101) — which Cruz voted against because it wasn't permanent. The honest counterweight: the $350,000 Jeff Yass-funded Bitcoin Freedom PAC contribution and the Armstrong/Winklevoss max donations that followed his positions in the most expensive Senate race ever ($192M raised). 26 cited sources.

- [Greg Abbott and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/greg-abbott-bitcoin): The Governor Who Took It First — the sourced twelve-year arc: the 2014 campaign accepting bitcoin donations (Apr 17, 2014, ~$2,000 collected, "The spirit of Bitcoin embodies the free market principles..."), the “Count me in as a crypto law proposal supporter” endorsement (Mar 2021), the legal foundation signed June 2021 (HB 4474 virtual-currency UCC + HB 1576 blockchain working group), the post-Uri recruitment of Bitcoin miners as controllable grid load (fall 2021), the SB 21 + HB 4488 signatures creating and shielding the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve (June 20, 2025), and the honest counterweight: the June 10, 2026 directive making data centers fund their own grid costs rather than residential ratepayers. 15 cited sources.

- [Dan Patrick and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/dan-patrick-bitcoin): The Asset, Not the Megawatts — the two-sided record resolved by its dates: the SB 1751 brake (Senate passage 30–1, Apr 12, 2023, the 10% demand-response cap that died in a House committee), the “Wild Wild West of data centers and crypto miners crashing our grid” warning (June 2024, ~2,600 MW mining load on ERCOT), then the pivot to the asset: Texas Bitcoin Reserve named a legislative priority (Jan 30, 2025), SB 21's bipartisan Senate passage (Mar 6, 2025) with the “digital gold” statement, and delivery (signed June 20, 2025). Thesis: bullish on the coin, tough on the load — one coherent position, not a flip. Honest counterweight: the industry's demand-response-is-a-service case against him. 12 cited sources.

- [Kelly Hancock and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/kelly-hancock-bitcoin): The Man Who Bought Texas Its Bitcoin — the execution record of the acting Texas Comptroller: succession from Glenn Hegar (chief clerk June 19, 2025; acting comptroller July 1, 2025, eleven days after SB 21), the first state Bitcoin purchase in U.S. history (~$5M in IBIT at $51.8694/share, Nov 20, 2025), the build to the full $10M appropriation, the advisory committee he chairs (four outside members named May 28, 2026) and custody RFP 908-26-1778WS (contract execution targeted late Aug 2026). Honest counterweight: the lame-duck steward — Hancock lost the Mar 3, 2026 GOP primary to Don Huffines (~58%–23%, Trump endorsement over Abbott's $2.6M in ads) and is finishing the custody transition for a successor (Huffines vs. Sarah Eckhardt, Nov 2026) to inherit in January 2027. 15 cited sources.

- [The Dead File: Texas Bitcoin Bills That Didn't Become Law](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-bills-that-died): The 89th Legislature's Bitcoin dead file, every status verified on capitol.texas.gov: HJR 175 (constitutional right to own/hold/use a chosen medium of exchange incl. digital currency - passed the House May 9, 2025, left pending in Senate Business & Commerce May 15); the kiosk stalemate (SB 1705 passed the Senate, died on the House calendar May 27; HB 2798 passed the House Apr 25, died in Senate committee - two majorities, zero laws, ~$57M/yr kiosk-scam losses since); the reserve designs not chosen (HB 1598 Capriglione in-treasury/5-yr hold/donations, no hearing; HB 4258 Reynolds/Plesa ~$250M + $10M local authority, no hearing; SB 778 superseded by SB 21); and what was cut from SB 21 itself (staking removed; $21M rider trimmed to $10M). Framed as the 90th Legislature's (Jan 2027) draft agenda - nothing was voted down. 13 cited sources.

## Data assets

- [Texas Bitcoin Mining Map](https://texasbitcoin.com/bitcoin-mining-map-texas): Interactive, sourced map and dataset of every major industrial Bitcoin mine in Texas — operator, capacity, year online, and AI/HPC conversions — plus the August 2026 ERCOT data-center queue audit (474 GW queue, "Batch Zero" paused) and the miner-built AI campuses it screens (Hut 8 Beacon Point, Cipher Barber Lake, MARA Matagorda). CC BY 4.0, 24 cited sources.
- [Texas Bitcoin Law Timeline](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-law-timeline): Interactive timeline of every Bitcoin law, memo, and failed bill in Texas — Supervisory Memorandum 1037 (2014) through SB 21's Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and HB 1056 (2025), each verified against capitol.texas.gov or dob.texas.gov. 22 cited sources.
- [Texas Bitcoin Case Tracker](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-case-tracker): Living, filterable dataset of every federal 18 U.S.C. § 1960 (unlicensed money transmission) and crypto prosecution announced in Texas's four federal districts — built nightly from public DOJ press releases, every case linked to its primary source. CC BY-SA 4.0.

## Stories

- [The Rockdale Story](https://texasbitcoin.com/rockdale-texas-bitcoin): How a dying aluminum town became the Bitcoin mining capital of North America — Alcoa (1952–2008), Bitmain, Whinstone, and Riot's 700 MW flagship, sourced end to end. 13 cited sources.
- [Doctor Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/doctor-bitcoin): Voices of Texas Bitcoin, No. 1 — the sourced profile of Mark Alexander Hopkins and the gap between Texas money-transmission law and federal FinCEN registration. 7 cited sources.
- [The Doctor Bitcoin Tapes](https://texasbitcoin.com/doctor-bitcoin-interviews): The lore companion to the profile — every interview Hopkins has given about his case (Digital Cash Network, Free Talk Live, the Aria DiMezzo prison conversation, Gary Leland's pre-case episodes) blended into one story, with the CZ proportionality ledger and sourced Crypto Six context. A living page awaiting Hopkins's own from-the-hip additions. 22 cited sources.

## Directories

- [Texas Bitcoin Events](https://texasbitcoin.com/events): Free, open directory of Bitcoin meetups and conferences across Austin, Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston, and San Antonio, linked directly to organizers.
- [Texas Bitcoin Resources](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-resources): Curated reference shelf of free tools for finding and understanding Bitcoin in Texas — merchant and community maps (BTC Map), the reachable-node census (bitnod.es), ERCOT grid data, and the state's policy bodies. Reference tools only: no exchanges, brokers, or referral links.

## Archive (direct link only)

- [The Wider Ledger — Texas Crypto Archive](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-crypto-archive): The wider Texas digital-asset story, kept off the main navigation by design — altcoins, developers, and venture capital: Factom's Bitcoin-anchored data layer from Austin (2014), hashgraph/Hedera born in Richardson's Telecom Corridor (2015), Multicoin Capital's early Solana call (2017), 8VC's HQ move to Austin (2020), ATX DAO's civic experiment (2021), the Austin City Council's twin crypto/blockchain resolutions (March 2022), and Consensus convening in Austin (2023–2024). 19 cited sources.
